topic: Microsoft Certified: Azure Administrator Associate (AZ-104) exam preparation - managing Azure identities and governance, implementing and managing storage, deploying and managing Azure compute resources, implementing and managing virtual networking, and monitoring and maintaining Azure resources
exam_format: Typically 40-60 questions in 100 minutes, delivered at Pearson VUE test centers or online-proctored. Question formats include multiple choice, multiple response, drag-and-drop, build-list, hot-area, and case studies. Scaled score 100-1000 with a passing score of 700 (700 does NOT mean 70 percent correct - it is a scaled threshold). The certification is valid for one year and is renewed free each year via a short online assessment on Microsoft Learn. Exam fee is approximately USD 165 and varies by country and local tax - present it as approximate and advise candidates to confirm current Microsoft pricing. Microsoft periodically updates the skills-measured outline (most recently in 2026), so tell candidates to verify the current domains and weights on the official Microsoft Learn AZ-104 page before scheduling.
question_types: multiple choice (single answer, exactly 4 options) and multiple response clearly marked 'Select TWO/THREE', plus scenario/case-study style items; every item is a real-world Azure administration scenario asking which service, setting, cmdlet, or configuration is correct - NOT term definitions
audience: Azure administrators who implement, manage, and monitor an organization's Microsoft Azure environment - identity, governance, storage, compute, virtual networking, and monitoring. Microsoft recommends 6+ months of hands-on Azure administration experience plus familiarity with the Azure portal, Azure CLI, Azure PowerShell, ARM/Bicep templates, and core concepts like RBAC and Azure Resource Manager. A strong companion to the AZ-305 (Solutions Architect Expert), AZ-204 (Developer Associate), and DP-600 (Fabric Analytics Engineer) courses already in this catalog.
author: Aseem Mankotia

domains.name: Manage Azure identities and governance
domains.notes: Managing Microsoft Entra ID (formerly Azure Active Directory) users and groups, administrative units, and device/registration settings; managing access with role-based access control (RBAC) built-in and custom roles at the correct scope (management group, subscription, resource group, resource); managing subscriptions and governance with management groups, Azure Policy (definitions, initiatives, exemptions, remediation), resource locks, and tags; and cost management with budgets and cost alerts. Choosing the correct identity, RBAC scope, or governance control for a described requirement, and distinguishing RBAC from Azure Policy and from Microsoft Entra roles.

domains.name: Implement and manage storage
domains.notes: Configuring storage accounts (performance tiers, redundancy LRS/ZRS/GRS/GZRS, access tiers hot/cool/cold/archive), securing access with access keys, shared access signatures (SAS), stored access policies, and Microsoft Entra authorization; configuring Azure Blob Storage (containers, lifecycle management, object replication, immutability), Azure Files and file shares (including Azure File Sync), and firewalls/virtual-network access; and using AzCopy and Storage Explorer. Choosing the correct redundancy option, access tier, or secure-access mechanism for a described scenario, and distinguishing SAS types and account vs service endpoints.

domains.name: Deploy and manage Azure compute resources
domains.notes: Deploying and managing virtual machines (sizes, availability sets and availability zones, disks and disk encryption, custom images, VM extensions); automating deployment with ARM templates and Bicep; configuring Virtual Machine Scale Sets and autoscale; deploying container workloads with Azure Container Instances and Azure Container Apps and managing Azure Container Registry; and configuring Azure App Service (plans, deployment slots, scaling, custom domains, TLS). Choosing the correct compute service, high-availability construct (availability set vs zone vs scale set), or deployment method for a described workload.

domains.name: Implement and manage virtual networking
domains.notes: Configuring virtual networks, subnets, and peering; name resolution with Azure DNS (public and private zones); securing traffic with network security groups (NSGs), application security groups, and Azure Bastion; configuring load balancing with Azure Load Balancer (public/internal, rules, health probes) and Azure Application Gateway; and configuring public IPs, routing (user-defined routes, service endpoints, private endpoints), and hybrid/VNet connectivity (VPN Gateway, virtual network gateways). Choosing the correct networking, load-balancing, or connectivity option for a described scenario, and distinguishing NSG vs Azure Firewall, Load Balancer vs Application Gateway, and service endpoints vs private endpoints.

domains.name: Monitor and maintain Azure resources
domains.notes: Monitoring with Azure Monitor (metrics, alerts, action groups), Log Analytics workspaces and Kusto Query Language (KQL) queries, Application Insights basics, Network Watcher (connection troubleshoot, NSG diagnostics, flow logs), and Azure Service Health; and implementing backup and recovery with Azure Backup (Recovery Services vault, backup policies) and Azure Site Recovery. Choosing the correct monitoring, alerting, or backup/recovery approach for a described operational or continuity requirement, and meeting a stated RPO/RTO.

extra_guidance: Microsoft Certified: Azure Administrator Associate (AZ-104) is Microsoft's core Azure operations credential and pairs directly with the AZ-305 architect and AZ-204 developer courses in this catalog. The exam is scenario-based - the real skill it tests is 'given this Azure administration situation, which service, setting, cmdlet, or configuration is correct,' NOT memorizing definitions. This is a READ-AND-UNDERSTAND administration course - show and explain real Azure portal steps, Azure CLI and Azure PowerShell commands, and ARM/Bicep and Azure Policy JSON exactly as they appear, rather than requiring a live paid Azure subscription; make that explicit (a free Azure account or the Microsoft Learn sandbox is enough to follow along). Use EXACT current Microsoft product names and call out recent renames: Microsoft Entra ID (formerly Azure Active Directory / Azure AD), Microsoft Entra roles, Azure RBAC, Azure Policy, management groups, Azure Resource Manager, Bicep, Azure Storage (Blob, Files, File Sync, lifecycle management, SAS), Azure Virtual Machines and Virtual Machine Scale Sets, Azure App Service, Azure Container Instances, Azure Container Apps, Azure Container Registry, Azure Virtual Network, network security groups, Azure Bastion, Azure Load Balancer, Azure Application Gateway, Azure Firewall, Azure DNS, VPN Gateway, Azure Monitor, Log Analytics, Kusto Query Language (KQL), Network Watcher, Azure Backup, Recovery Services vault, and Azure Site Recovery - with a one-line note that Azure evolves fast, so verify against current Microsoft Learn docs. The five domain names and weight RANGES above are Microsoft's official AZ-104 skills-measured groupings - present the ranges as Microsoft does and note Microsoft updates weights periodically. Cover the classic AZ-104 traps: RBAC vs Azure Policy vs Microsoft Entra roles, RBAC scope inheritance, storage redundancy (LRS/ZRS/GRS/GZRS) and access tiers, SAS types (account vs service vs user delegation), availability sets vs availability zones vs scale sets, NSG vs Azure Firewall, Azure Load Balancer vs Application Gateway (Layer 4 vs Layer 7), service endpoints vs private endpoints, VNet peering vs VPN gateway, and Azure Backup vs Azure Site Recovery. NEVER promise a pass or use the word 'guarantee' in ANY form (Udemy compliance) - use 'exam-focused preparation' framing throughout, including the learning objectives and who-this-is-for. Present the exam fee as approximate (~USD 165, varies by country) and note the certification is valid one year with free annual renewal on Microsoft Learn. The final chapter must be a full exam simulation with a 100-minute, ~40-60-question time-management strategy that accounts for case studies. Scan the practice bank for stray other-vendor terms (AWS/Google/NVIDIA) before upload per the pipeline compliance rules.
